inspection_outcome: One verified central construction error and one auxiliary proof qualification
summary: The general cell-boundary SDP construction uses a false common-face distance formula whose derivative is also wrong in a finite CAT(0) four-square example. Core Hadamard recognition and maximal-cell interior mechanisms survived bounded checks. Auxiliary primal-attainment proof confuses selected-bicombing and all-geodesics convexity.
limitations: Exact acquired arXiv 2406.03913v1 only; journal-final persistence unknown
No wrong final recognition decision or impossible semidefinite representation asserted
No theorem-wide falsity or whole-paper verification asserted

problems.title: False common-face distance and derivative construction

source_claim.locator: Section 11, PDF p35 common-face formula; dependency pp36–37; cell definitions p27
source_claim.text: For incident cells C,Q_a and F_a=C intersect Q_a, every geodesic from x_a to y in C crosses F_a, yielding a minimum of two within-cell lengths used to construct the directional derivative SDP.

assumptions: Finite complete CAT(0) cubical complex X=[-1,1]^2 with four unit squares
a=x_a=(-1/2,-1/2), y=(1/2,1/4); initial segment lies wholly in Q_a

check.type: Exact Euclidean counterexample and derivative calculation
steps: Face expression=sqrt(2)/2+sqrt(5)/4>5/4 because straight segment does not pass through 0.
For u=e1, true d_a(tu)=sqrt((t+1/2)^2+1/4), derivative at0=1/sqrt(2).
Face expression sqrt(2)/2+t has derivative1. Scaling/shortening does not remove discrepancy.
check.result: Printed formula and derived directional derivative are false under the stated general hypotheses.

counterevidence: Both displayed derivatives are positive: no erroneous final decision demonstrated.
Relative-interior construction has separate valid Euclidean-neighborhood argument.
Tripod paths cross common vertex and exact certificate condition w_i<=1/2 agrees with genuine derivatives.

impact.dependency: p35 face formula -> distance SDR -> subdifferential/support fa,C -> P_C SDP -> pp36–37 certificate sets
impact.scope: Materially invalidates stated general construction supporting a core advertised boundary algorithm; does not refute general mean recognition, every boundary case, or possibility of another SDP.

correction.statement: Require geodesic passage through the common face, or replace construction with one that accounts for intervening cells.
correction.verification: Under actual passage hypothesis triangle inequality and split-geodesic lengths prove equality. Exact tripod check verifies a valid branching case.
correction.limits: No general replacement derivative representation or computational complexity established.

independent_verification.result: Confirmed under the actual finite CAT(0) cubical definition and maximal-cell restriction. In the four-square Euclidean complex the true distance is 5/4, whereas forcing a route through the single common vertex gives sqrt(2)/2+sqrt(5)/4. Along e1 at the origin the true derivative is 1/sqrt(2), the constructed one 1. Pages35-37 explicitly use this formula through distance/subdifferential/support representations to f_a,C, P_C and V_C. Shortening or scaling preserves the derivative defect. Both signs in the displayed direction remain positive, so no final recognition error is inferred.

problems.title: Selected-bicombing convexity does not imply all-geodesics convexity

source_claim.locator: PDF p11 convex-set definition; Definitions4.1–4.2 and Theorem4.3 pp12–13; Assumption3.1 p8
source_claim.text: The proof declares every F_k convex after showing preservation only along the chosen conical bicombing and then invokes reflexivity.

assumptions: X=(R^2,l_infinity), A={0}, p=1, Y=R, G=identity, c=1,b=0
Strict primal and dual feasible via xhat0,yhat1,what1
Proper finite-dimensional space and linear conical bicombing; nu0 and F_k=[-r,r]^2,r=1/k

steps: gamma(s)=(-r+2rs,r+2r min(s,1-s)) joins two top corners of F_k.
First-coordinate differences equal2r|s-t| and second differences are at most that, so gamma is a constant-speed geodesic.
check.result: The intermediate all-geodesics convexity assertion is false; the displayed proof does not justify invoking its stated reflexivity.

counterevidence: The primal optimum in this example is attained.
Main Theorem6.1 explicitly avoids reliance on general primal attainment.

impact.dependency: Auxiliary Theorem4.3 F_k convexity -> reflexive intersection -> primal attainment
impact.scope: Limited general proof qualification; not failure of main Hadamard recognition or a nonattainment counterexample.

correction.statement: Restrict to uniquely geodesic spaces with the stated bicombing, or assume nested intersection for chosen-bicombing-convex sets.
correction.verification: Then the proved F_k convexity is exactly the kind to which the intersection assumption applies.
correction.limits: Does not show original general hypotheses already imply that condition.

independent_verification.result: Confirmed from the definition requiring all geodesics and the proof using one selected bicombing. In l_infinity^2, the stated constant-speed path leaves the square F_k at its midpoint while satisfying the source's feasibility, properness and conical-bicombing assumptions. The example attains its optimum; source p12 expressly separates main mean-set equivalence from general primal attainment. Unique geodesics or the stated stronger intersection assumption give sufficient, explicitly additional repairs.
